extraction.summary: The authors define vacuum by Ť^μ_ν = −V δ^μ_ν, so its covariant transfer is fixed as Q_ν = −∇_νV and total conservation requires the opposite transfer in matter. A single perfect-fluid dark-energy stress tensor admits the exact algebraic split ρ_m = ρ_de + P_de, V = −P_de, but that background/stress-tensor identity does not choose a perturbation theory. For a generalized Chaplygin gas the homogeneous split gives Q = 3αHρ_mV/(ρ_m+V). Two perturbative lifts are then distinguished: geodesic transfer Q^μ = Q u^μ has no comoving vacuum force and zero effective rest-frame pressure response, while a separate local-function closure with constant A recovers the barotropic Chaplygin perturbations and their adiabatic sound speed. The same background can therefore represent different perturbation physics. The paper supplies formal equations and a proposed route to observations, not a fit or a qualified observational result.

ideas.title: Inhomogeneous vacuum is fixed by a gradient transfer and selects uniform-vacuum slices
ideas.description: Because the vacuum stress tensor is proportional to the metric, its divergence is Q_ν = −∇_νV. A conserved total stress tensor gives matter the opposite transfer. Where ∇V is nonzero and non-null, the normalized gradient defines a preferred potential-flow direction and hypersurfaces of uniform V; the vacuum itself has no unique material four-velocity. The special closure Q^μ = Q u^μ identifies that flow with matter and therefore restricts the matter flow to be irrotational.
locators: Sec. II, Eqs. (1)-(8), PDF p. 2, HTML #S2.E1, #S2.E2, #S2.E6, #S2.E7, #S2.E8
Sec. III.A, Eqs. (9)-(11), PDF p. 2, HTML #S3.E9 and #S3.EGx1

equations.definitions: Mixed-index stress tensors; metric signature is (−,+,+,+) in Eq. (12). Vacuum density is V and vacuum pressure is −V. Matter is a perfect fluid with density ρ, pressure P, and unit four-velocity u^μ.
equations.units: With c=1, V, ρ and P have energy-density units; u^μ is normalized as a four-velocity.
equations.domain: Einstein gravity and the assumed perfect-fluid matter stress tensor.

equations.locator: Sec. II, Eqs. (5)-(8), PDF p. 2, HTML #S2.E5-#S2.E8
equations.definitions: Q_ν is defined as the divergence of the vacuum stress tensor; the second equality assumes covariant conservation of the total matter-plus-vacuum stress tensor.
equations.units: Q_ν is an energy-density gradient; in FRW the scalar Q has energy-density per time units.
equations.domain: Einstein gravity with conserved total stress energy. A non-interacting vacuum has ∇_νV=0.

equations.locator: Sec. III.A, Eqs. (10)-(11), PDF p. 2, HTML #S3.EGx1
equations.definitions: The paper's sign convention makes positive Q increase vacuum energy and remove energy from matter; Q_ν=Q u_ν in the homogeneous isotropic background.

equations.locator: Sec. II, Eq. (7), PDF p. 2, HTML #S2.E7
equations.definitions: The paper's normalized energy-flow direction, not a unique vacuum particle velocity; its integral slices have uniform V.
equations.units: Dimensionless normalized four-vector in c=1 units.
equations.domain: Requires a nonzero non-null vacuum gradient; the paper does not discuss a null-gradient normalization.

ideas.title: Vacuum perturbations have gauge-invariant relative entropy, conditional on the interaction closure
ideas.description: The vacuum perturbation has zero intrinsic nonadiabatic pressure, but its density perturbation on matter-comoving slices is generally nonzero and equals the background transfer rate times the relative matter/energy-flow velocity potential. It vanishes on energy-flow-orthogonal slices by construction. The total nonadiabatic pressure includes a relative vacuum-fluid entropy term, so a vacuum-plus-matter split does not by itself force nonadiabaticity: it vanishes for the specified adiabatic conditions or Q=0. If V is a local function of the matter density, the relative entropy vanishes.
locators: Sec. III.B, Eqs. (15)-(23), PDF p. 3, HTML #S3.EGx2-#S3.EGx5
Sec. III.C, Eqs. (24)-(30), PDF p. 4, HTML #S3.E24-#S3.E30

equations.expression: δρ̌_com = δV + V̇θ = V̇(θ−θ̌); Δρ̌_com = δV + V̇θ̌ = 0
equations.locator: Sec. III.C, Eqs. (25)-(27), PDF p. 4, HTML #S3.E25-#S3.E27
equations.definitions: θ is the matter velocity potential; θ̌ is the energy-flow potential and transforms the same way under a time-slicing change. The relative velocity is gauge invariant.
equations.units: δV is an energy density; θ and θ̌ have time units in the paper's cosmic-time conventions.
equations.domain: Linear scalar perturbations about spatially flat FRW; θ̌ = −δV/V̇ where V̇ is nonzero.

equations.locator: Sec. III.C, Eq. (29), PDF p. 4, HTML #S3.E29
equations.definitions: Relative entropy between vacuum and fluid, expressed on uniform-fluid-density slices; ζ̌ = −ψ−HδV/V̇ and ζ is the corresponding fluid curvature perturbation.
equations.domain: Linear scalar perturbations where the background derivatives in the ratios are nonzero.

equations.locator: Sec. III.C, Eq. (30), PDF p. 4, HTML #S3.E30
equations.definitions: The paper defines c_s² = Ṗ/ρ̇ as the adiabatic sound speed in Eq. (17); Š is the relative vacuum-fluid entropy. The displayed extra term is conditional on the interaction and entropy perturbation.
equations.units: Each term is a pressure perturbation; c_s² and Š are dimensionless.
equations.domain: Linear scalar perturbations with the stated perfect-fluid and transfer decomposition; the expression's denominators must be nonzero.

ideas.title: A perfect-fluid dark-energy stress tensor can be split algebraically into dust and vacuum
ideas.description: For one dark-energy component already described by the perfect-fluid tensor, the exact same tensor is obtained with pressureless matter sharing its four-velocity plus vacuum energy when ρ_m=ρ_de+P_de and V=−P_de. The induced covariant transfer is Q_μ=∇_μP_de, hence Q=−Ṗ_de in FRW. This is an algebraic identity at the tensor level; it does not uniquely lift a chosen background history into perturbations or give a microphysical interaction. Splitting into two generic fluids would introduce an unconstrained extra degree of freedom.
locators: Sec. IV.B, Eq. (33) and immediately following text, PDF p. 5, HTML #S4.E33

equations.expression: ρ_m = ρ_de + P_de; V = −P_de; Q_μ = ∇_μP_de; Q = −Ṗ_de in FRW
equations.locator: Sec. IV.B, Eq. (33) and following sentence, PDF p. 5, HTML #S4.E33
equations.definitions: ρ_de and P_de are the original single perfect-fluid dark-energy density and pressure; the pressureless component shares its velocity. The Q_μ relation follows from Q_μ=−∇_μV.
equations.units: ρ_m, V and P_de have energy-density units; Q has energy-density per time units.
equations.domain: A single perfect-fluid stress tensor with no separately represented anisotropic stress or additional components. The identity alone says nothing about the perturbative closure.

ideas.title: The generalized Chaplygin background admits a one-parameter interacting-vacuum form
ideas.description: Applying the algebraic split to P_gCg=−Aρ_gCg^(−α) yields the standard homogeneous density solution, a vacuum contribution V, the relation A=(ρ_m+V)^αV, and Q=3αHρ_mV/(ρ_m+V). In this interaction parameterization α is the dimensionless coupling and A can arise as an integration constant depending on initial conditions. The paper quotes earlier observational constraints on the barotropic sound-speed model but performs no fit. The limit α→0 recovers the successful ΛCDM background/perturbation limit discussed by the authors; the source supplies no broader allowed α interval.
locators: Sec. IV.B, Eqs. (34)-(38), PDF pp. 5-6, HTML #S4.E34-#S4.E38

equations.locator: Sec. IV.B, Eqs. (34)-(35), PDF p. 5, HTML #S4.E34-#S4.E35
equations.definitions: A and B are constants in the barotropic solution; α is dimensionless; a is the scale factor.
equations.units: A and B have units of energy-density^(1+α) when a is dimensionless; ρ and P have energy-density units.
equations.domain: As written the power-law solution excludes α=−1 and requires a real positive branch; the paper does not state a full parameter/sign domain.

equations.locator: Sec. IV.B, Eqs. (37)-(38), PDF p. 5, HTML #S4.E37-#S4.E38
equations.definitions: ρ_m is the pressureless component, V is vacuum density, and Q follows the paper's convention V̇=Q. A has the same dimensional role as in the barotropic equation of state.
equations.units: Q has energy-density per time units; α is dimensionless.
equations.domain: Homogeneous Chaplygin solution and its algebraic matter-vacuum decomposition; no α fit or viability interval is established.

ideas.title: Geodesic and barotropic covariant lifts share a background but have different perturbations
ideas.description: The authors consider at least two covariant extensions of the same FRW interaction. With Q^μ=Q u^μ, the energy flow follows matter, δV=−Qθ, the Euler equation is geodesic, and there is no comoving vacuum force or pressure perturbation, giving zero effective rest-frame sound speed. This restricts the matter velocity to be irrotational and the authors say they lack a clear covariant model for the scalar Q. Their alternative Q_μ=−∇_μ[A/(ρ_m+V)^α] reduces to the background interaction when Ȧ=0; when A is a universal constant it enforces the barotropic Chaplygin relation and Š=0, so the full perturbations are exactly those of that barotropic fluid, with generally nonzero adiabatic sound speed. Eq. (43) parameterizes the geodesic relative entropy by a spatially varying local δA and is singular as written at α=0.
locators: Sec. IV.B, Eqs. (39)-(44), PDF p. 6, HTML #S4.EGx6-#S4.EGx7 and #S4.E43-#S4.E44

equations.expression: Q^μ = Q u^μ; θ̌=θ; δV=−Qθ; θ̇+φ=0
equations.locator: Sec. IV.B, discussion and Eqs. (39)-(40), PDF p. 6, HTML #S4.EGx6
equations.definitions: Geodesic energy transfer along the pressureless matter four-velocity; the velocity potential is θ and the lapse perturbation is φ.
equations.units: θ has time units; δV is an energy density.
equations.domain: Linear scalar perturbations. The common flow is potential/irrotational; no covariant scalar closure for Q is supplied.

equations.locator: Sec. IV.B, Eq. (43) and following sentence, PDF p. 6, HTML #S4.E43
equations.definitions: δA is a local perturbation of the integration-constant relation A=(ρ_m+V)^αV; in the geodesic case it represents relative entropy/local equation-of-state variation.
equations.units: Š and δA/A are dimensionless; δP_nad has pressure units.
equations.domain: The displayed parameterization requires α, ρ_m, and ρ_m+(1+α)V nonzero. It cannot be naively evaluated at α=0.

equations.expression: Q_μ = −∇_μ[A/(ρ_m+V)^α]; if ∇_μA=0 then Š=0 and the full model is barotropic Chaplygin
equations.locator: Sec. IV.B, Eq. (44) and following text, PDF p. 6, HTML #S4.E44
equations.definitions: The authors' alternative covariant choice for the energy flow; exact barotropic equivalence is stated for universal constant A.
equations.units: The bracket has energy-density units; its gradient has transfer-vector units.
equations.domain: The stated FRW reduction assumes Ȧ=0; the exact perturbative equivalence claim further assumes ∇_μA=0.

equations.locator: Reader algebra from Sec. IV.B, Eqs. (34), (37), and (44), PDF pp. 5-6
equations.definitions: Adiabatic derivative for the constant-A barotropic Chaplygin closure, not the effective rest-frame sound speed assigned to the geodesic closure.
equations.domain: Constant-A barotropic branch with nonzero total density; this is a symbolic consequence of the stated equation of state, not a fitted value.

ideas.title: Scalar-field potential energy is a familiar vacuum-matter transfer with an underlying field equation
ideas.description: For a scalar Lagrangian L=F(X)−V(φ), the kinetic stress tensor transfers energy to the potential through Q_μ=−(∂V/∂φ)∇_μφ. Its conservation reproduces the generalized Klein-Gordon equation. The authors use this as a microphysically specified example and distinguish it from the phenomenological pressureless-matter interaction, for which no action is supplied.
locators: Sec. IV.A, Eqs. (31)-(32), PDF pp. 4-5, HTML #S4.E31-#S4.E32

equations.locator: Sec. IV.A, text before Eq. (31), PDF p. 4, HTML #S4.E31 context
equations.definitions: F is a kinetic function and V(φ) a scalar potential; X is the canonical kinetic invariant.
equations.units: Natural units; the Lagrangian density and V have energy-density units.
equations.domain: Single scalar field with the stated Lagrangian form.

equations.locator: Sec. IV.A, Eq. (32), PDF p. 5, HTML #S4.E32
equations.definitions: Generalized Klein-Gordon equation obtained from kinetic-sector energy conservation with the vacuum transfer.
equations.units: Terms have matching scalar-field equation units under the paper's action conventions.
equations.domain: Single scalar field and differentiable F(X), V(φ).

ideas.title: A matched-background linear growth and potential comparison can distinguish the closures
ideas.description: The smallest useful comparison suggested by the paper is to hold the same Chaplygin-derived H(a) and background component densities fixed, impose matched initial conditions, then compare the linear comoving matter-density growth, velocity evolution, and metric-potential evolution under the geodesic and constant-A barotropic closures. The geodesic branch has a pressureless Euler equation and no comoving vacuum force; the barotropic branch has its adiabatic sound-speed response. A resulting scale-dependent growth/potential difference could be mapped to RSD or lensing/ISW observables only after a complete baryon, radiation, and observation model is specified. This is a proposed falsifiable comparison, not a calculation or a result of this paper.
locators: Inference from Sec. III.B, Eqs. (20)-(23), PDF p. 3; Sec. IV.B, Eqs. (39)-(44), PDF p. 6

equations.expression: Compare Eq. (21) with the geodesic Euler equation (40) and the constant-A barotropic closure (44), at fixed background solution (35)-(38)
equations.locator: Reader inference from PDF pp. 3, 5-6, Eqs. (21), (35)-(40), (44)
equations.definitions: Proposed comparison holds background expansion and initial perturbations fixed while changing the covariant perturbation closure; observable mapping remains unspecified.
equations.units: Dimensionless density contrasts and metric potentials; velocity/growth quantities require the stated time or scale-factor convention.
equations.domain: Would require a complete linear multi-component perturbation model and specified observation/likelihood lineage; not evaluated in the paper.

quantities.conditioning: Symbolic model parameter in Eqs. (34)-(38); the paper reports no fitted value or allowed interval. The authors discuss α→0 as the ΛCDM limit.

quantities.name: A, Chaplygin equation-of-state constant
quantities.conditioning: No numerical value is reported. In the homogeneous interaction-only parameterization it can emerge as an integration constant; the alternative covariant closure Eq. (44) includes A explicitly.

quantities.name: Effective rest-frame sound speed squared in geodesic matter-vacuum closure
quantities.conditioning: Author-stated consequence of Q^μ=Qu^μ and vanishing comoving vacuum force for the linear interacting pressureless-matter plus vacuum model; not an observational estimate.

quantities.conditioning: Reader algebra from dP/dρ for Eq. (34) and A=(ρ_m+V)^αV; symbolic and model-conditioned, not fitted. This quantity must not be identified with the geodesic branch's effective rest-frame sound speed.

data_dependencies.detail: This paper presents analytical background and linear-perturbation equations; it reports no newly fitted parameters, data likelihood, or original observational dataset.

The authors state that barotropic generalized Chaplygin models are strongly constrained and that the successful ΛCDM limit is α→0. This paper does not specify or re-audit the underlying data, calibration, covariance, fitter, or likelihood.

Cited as prior generalized-Chaplygin and matter-vacuum decomposition work; no new data lineage is established here. Of these prior-foundation references, [40] is currently registered in Prospector; [43] is not.

caveats: The identity ρ_m=ρ_de+P_de and V=−P_de is exact for the stated single perfect-fluid stress tensor, but it does not establish equivalence between distinct covariant perturbation closures.
The geodesic closure Q^μ=Qu^μ implies a potential, irrotational matter flow, excludes generic vorticity, and is not supplied with a clear covariant scalar law for Q by the authors.
The alternative local-function transfer becomes exactly barotropic only with universal constant A. The background interaction alone does not enforce this closure.

The paper distinguishes adiabatic c_s²=Ṗ/ρ̇ from the zero effective rest-frame pressure response of the geodesic branch. Treating these as the same sound speed would erase the physical distinction between the closures.

Equation (43) is a parameterization of relative entropy via δA/A and is singular as written at α=0 and at its other denominator zeros; the α→0 limit must be taken from the underlying equations, not this expression.
The source gives no general α stability or sign domain and does not single out α=−1/2. Equation (35) itself has a special α=−1 exponent case that is not discussed.
The normalized flow vector in Eq. (7) requires a non-null gradient. Degenerate constant or null-gradient cases are not separately developed.

The perturbation treatment is first-order scalar perturbation theory around spatially flat FRW in Einstein gravity. There is no nonlinear completion or full multi-component cosmological implementation here.

No action or microphysical mechanism for the Chaplygin matter-vacuum interaction is derived. The scalar-field section is a familiar field-theory example, not a derivation of the Chaplygin transfer law.
Statements about observational constraints are literature-context statements; no independent observational reassessment, reproduction, or scientific qualification was performed in this reading.

usefulness.assessment: High value as a formal bridge and a warning against promoting a background decomposition to perturbative equivalence. The most reusable result is the explicit separation between the geodesic zero-rest-pressure closure and the constant-A barotropic Chaplygin closure.
usefulness.transferable_relation: A dark perfect fluid can be algebraically represented by dust plus vacuum while preserving its total stress tensor; an interaction four-vector prescription is still needed to fix inhomogeneous behavior.
usefulness.most_useful_distinction: Same FRW Q(a) and H(a) can coexist with inequivalent perturbations. Geodesic transfer imposes irrotational flow and zero comoving vacuum force, whereas constant-A gradient transfer enforces Š=0 and exact barotropic sound-speed behavior.
usefulness.smallest_falsifiable_comparison: At fixed background and matched initial conditions, compare linear comoving matter growth, velocity, and metric potentials between the two closures; then specify an observable mapping such as RSD or lensing/ISW with a complete component and data model. This is only an inference from the equations and was not calculated.
usefulness.readiness: Source-reading packet only. It is not a Sol-reviewed idea, accepted prospect, executable candidate design, independent reproduction, or observational qualification.
